title: Viewing the targets
summary: How the targets are shown before shooting in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting, which doubles you see, and what you may do while they fly.

body.html: Before shooting, the targets are shown: this is the presentation. In Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ it happens on each stand. In Compak® Sporting by squad, where a squad of at most six shooters moves along the stations, it happens only once a day, for the first squad. In line it works differently (see below). The presentation lets you read each target: its line, speed and distance, and what the clay does in the air.

html.sporting: On each stand, the first shooter of the squad sees all the trajectories, standing ready on the stand.
html.compak: By squad: only once a day, in the morning, for the day's first squad. The shooter on station 1 calls singles A to F. In line: see below.

body.html: You may ask the referee to show a target again: at most two more times for each target on the stand's menu.

Doubles on report (the second target leaves when you fire at the first) are not shown. You have already seen their targets, though: a double only uses targets thrown as singles from the same stand. The first shooter of each squad is shown the simultaneous doubles (both targets leave together) and rafale doubles (two targets from the same trap, one after the other). On request they are shown again, at most twice.
By squad, the singles are followed by the simultaneous doubles of stations 1 to 5. After that you will hear 'start' or 'competition' from the referee, and the scored shooting begins.

Compak® Sporting can also be shot in line: shooters step onto station 1 one by one and move along the line to station 5. Before the start, the first shooter may ask to see singles A to F; with simultaneous doubles, the doubles of each station are shown too. While the line fills up, each new shooter on station 1 first sees the opening target of their double. As the line empties, the referee does the same at the later stations. Details: Chapter 17 · In line with doubles on report, Chapter 17 · In line with simultaneous doubles, Chapter 17 · Closing the line.
In both disciplines, guns stay open and unloaded during the presentation and any interruption. Close yours only when the referee allows it.

Firing, or mock shooting (mounting and swinging the gun along the target's line without a shot), while the targets are shown is forbidden. It is penalised like a gun-position offence: a warning first, then a red card.

html.sporting: If a trap breaks down or shooting stops for more than 10 minutes, the stand's targets are shown again.
html.compak: After a break of more than 10 minutes, the referee shows the six singles once more.

html.sporting: Nobody may practise on the competition layouts.
html.compak: You may practise on the competition trajectories, but not with the competition menus. The trajectory setting tables (ready-made menus that say which traps are shot from each station) must be different for practice. At continental and world championships, the official practice starts on the Saturday before the event.

body.html: Use the presentation to plan each target. Note where you will first see it clearly, the pick-up point, and where you will break it, the break point. Many coaches suggest also choosing the order for a simultaneous double while you watch.
How to read a target from the presentation: How to read a target.

notes.html: In training, viewing is the coach's favourite moment: 'watch where it turns'. In competition the presentation is part of the event, so the coaching ban applies: stay quiet unless the referee or the shooter needs a translation of procedure.

key_points.html: Sporting™: on each stand, the first shooter of the squad sees all the trajectories, standing ready.
Sporting™: on request, up to two repeats for each target of the menu.
Sporting™: doubles on report are not presented; the first shooter of each squad sees the simultaneous and rafale doubles.

Compak® Sporting by squad: the targets are presented once a day, in the morning, for the first squad only. After a break of more than 10 minutes, the referee presents the six singles once more. In line has its own order.
Guns stay open during the presentation; in Sporting™, firing or mock shooting at that time is penalised.

did_you_know.html: In Sporting™ the menu in front of each stand lists the traps in shooting order and marks special targets, such as a battue or a rabbit.

quiz.q: In Sporting™, which doubles are NOT shown at the presentation?
quiz.explain: In Sporting™ doubles on report are not presented; simultaneous and rafale doubles are. A double only uses targets already thrown as singles on that stand.

quiz.q: In Compak® Sporting by squad, how often are the targets presented?

options.text: Before each squad, on each station
Once a day, for the first squad
Only when a shooter asks for it

quiz.explain: There is one presentation a day, in the morning, for the first squad; after a break of more than 10 minutes the referee presents the six singles once more.

quiz.q: In Sporting™, during the presentation a shooter closes the gun and swings along a target's line. What applies?

options.text: Forbidden: a warning, then a red card
Only the coach gets a warning

quiz.explain: Guns stay open during the presentation, and firing or mock shooting is penalised like a gun-position offence.
